neighbours.label: the verb or adverb inside a future-tense clause after 'will' / 'going to' ('will find', 'by then')
fire: The manager promised, "We will see what we can do next week."
Don't worry, the police will find your bike eventually.
I will finish the report by Friday, I promise.
Next season the club is going to sign two new strikers.
She said the results will arrive by the end of the month.
Tomorrow we will learn who won the election.
The engineers will test the bridge again in the spring.
After the break, you will know exactly what to do.
quiet: The manager said, "We saw what we could do last week."
Don't worry, the police found your bike yesterday.
I finished the report on Friday, as I promised.
Last season the club signed two new strikers.
She said the results arrived at the end of the month.
Yesterday we learned who won the election.
The engineers tested the bridge again in the spring.
After the break, you knew exactly what to do.

notes: card: broad flag, gate-closed 68%, small max; peaks ' find', ' see', ' where', ' by' after 'will'. Probe: 'We will find' 0.55 vs 'We found' 0.10
